Final review complete. The fix in `src/dotenv/main.py` (set_key, lines 184-187) escapes backslashes before apostrophes when quoting:

```python
if quote:
    value_out = "'{}'".format(
        value_to_set.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")
    )
```

Verified correct against the parser: `_single_quoted_value` (parser.py:25) and `_single_quote_escapes` (parser.py:32, `\\[\\']`) with `decode_escapes` (parser.py:105-109) form the exact inverse. Escaping order is right (backslashes doubled first, then apostrophes), so consecutive backslashes and apostrophes round-trip through `dotenv_values(interpolate=False)`. Existing quote modes (`always`/`auto`/`never`) and `export` behavior are preserved. All host acceptance and upstream regression tests passed; no further edits were needed.

Remaining limitations (pre-existing, out of scope): `quote_mode="never"` performs no escaping, and the parser's `unicode-escape` decoding interprets sequences like `\n` in single-quoted values as a newline on read.
